title: They Said France Was Overrated... Until They Saw These 20 Places
tags: France travel guide|best places in France|French Alps hiking|Provence lavender fields|Loire Valley castles|Bordeaux wine tours|Mont Saint Michel tips|Alsace Christmas markets|Dordogne prehistoric caves|Carcassonne medieval city|Lyon food capital|Marseille coastal hikes|Rocamadour pilgrimage site|Normandy D-Day beaches|Corsica beaches|Annecy lake activities|Saint Emilion wine tasting|Giverny Monet gardens|Brittany coastal towns|France road trip|TBT|tbt
description:
France is a treasure trove of iconic cities, picturesque villages, and breathtaking landscapes. Here’s a curated list of 20 must see places to visit in France, blending famous landmarks with hidden gems, based on expert recommendations and traveler favorites:

Paris:
The "City of Light" tops every list with its timeless allure—Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Notre-Dame (reopened post-2024 renovations). Stroll Montmartre or sip coffee at a sidewalk café for quintessential Parisian charm.

French Alps (Chamonix-Mont-Blanc):
Home to Europe’s highest peak, Mont Blanc, this region offers world-class skiing, hiking, and alpine villages like Annecy, the "Venice of the Alps".

French Riviera (Côte d’Azur):
From glamorous Nice and Cannes to hilltop Èze and Menton’s lemon groves, the Riviera blends beaches, art (Matisse Museum), and luxury.

Loire Valley:
A UNESCO-listed region dotted with fairy-tale châteaux (Chenonceau, Chambord) and vineyards. Perfect for cycling and garden tours.

Provence:
Lavender fields, Roman ruins (Pont du Gard), and villages like Gordes and Roussillon define this sun-drenched region. Don’t miss Aix-en-Provence’s Cézanne trail.

Bordeaux:
Wine lovers rejoice! Explore grand châteaux, La Cité du Vin, and the neoclassical Place de la Bourse. Pair with a trip to Dune du Pilat, Europe’s tallest sand dune.

Mont Saint-Michel:
This tidal island abbey in Normandy is a Gothic masterpiece, especially magical at sunrise or lit at night.

Alsace (Colmar & Strasbourg):
Half-timbered houses, canals (Petite France), and Christmas markets make Colmar and Strasbourg storybook destinations. Wine routes add to the charm.

Dordogne Valley:
Prehistoric caves (Lascaux), medieval towns (Sarlat), and canoeing past castles like Beynac create a rustic adventure.

Carcassonne:
A fully walled medieval city with turrets and cobblestone lanes—best explored at dawn or dusk to avoid crowds.

Champagne Region:
Tour Reims’ cathedral and Épernay’s champagne houses (Moët & Chandon) along the Avenue de Champagne.

Lyon:
France’s gastronomic capital boasts bouchons, silk history, and Roman amphitheaters. A quieter alternative to Paris.

Marseille:
Vibrant port city with calanques (cliff-lined coves), multicultural cuisine, and the Mucem museum.

Rocamadour:
A cliffside pilgrimage site in the Lot Valley, famed for its cheese and dramatic setting.

Normandy’s D-Day Beaches:
Historic WWII sites like Omaha Beach and the Bayeux Tapestry offer poignant insight.

Corsica:
Wild beaches (Palombaggia), mountain trails, and Bonifacio’s cliffside old town showcase its rugged beauty.

Annecy:
Crystal-clear lake, flower-lined canals, and alpine vistas make this town a year-round gem.

Saint-Émilion:
A Bordeaux-region medieval village surrounded by vineyards, perfect for wine tastings.

Giverny:
Monet’s home and water lily gardens, immortalized in his paintings, are a serene escape.

Brittany (Saint-Malo & Cancale):
Fortified coastal towns, oyster farms, and the Pink Granite Coast offer Celtic-flavored charm.

Pro Tip: For fewer crowds, visit popular spots like Paris in winter or the Riviera in shoulder seasons (March–April or September–October)

description:
Germany is a treasure trove of history, culture, natural beauty, and modern marvels. Here’s a list of 20 must-see places you should visit as a traveler before you die:

1. Neuschwanstein Castle:
The fairy-tale castle that inspired Disney’s Sleeping Beauty Castle, nestled in the Bavarian Alps.

2. Brandenburg Gate:
 Berlin’s iconic symbol of unity and history, a must-see at night when lit up.

3. Cologne Cathedral:
A stunning Gothic masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

4. The Romantic Road:
A scenic route through medieval towns like Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Füssen, and Würzburg.

5. The Black Forest:
Dense forests, charming villages (like Triberg with its waterfalls), and the home of the cuckoo clock.

6. Oktoberfest:
The world’s largest beer festival (late September to early October).

7. Zugspitze:
Stunning alpine views, accessible by cable car or cogwheel train.

8. Heidelberg Old Town & Castle:
A romantic university town with a ruined castle overlooking the Neckar River.

9. The Berlin Wall & East Side Gallery:
The longest open-air gallery featuring murals on a surviving stretch of the Wall.

10. Sanssouci Palace:
 Frederick the Great’s stunning Rococo palace and gardens.

11. Bamberg:
A UNESCO-listed medieval town famous for its smoked beer (Rauchbier) and stunning cathedral.

12. The Rhine Valley:
A UNESCO site with castles, vineyards, and the Lorelei Rock—best explored by river cruise.

13. Nuremberg Christmas Market:
One of the oldest and most magical Christmas markets in the world.

14. Dresden’s Frauenkirche & Zwinger Palace:
A baroque masterpiece, rebuilt after WWII destruction.

15. Lübeck:
 A medieval Hanseatic city famous for its marzipan and stunning Holstentor gate.

16. Berchtesgaden National Park & Königssee:
Crystal-clear alpine lake with St. Bartholomä Church and breathtaking hikes.

17. Miniatur Wunderland:
 The world’s largest model railway museum—a delight for all ages.

18. Rügen Island:
Germany’s largest island with chalk cliffs (Jasmund National Park) and Baltic Sea beaches.

19. The Moselle Valley:
A picturesque wine region with steep vineyards and charming towns like Cochem.

20. Eltz Castle:
A hidden medieval gem tucked in a forest, one of Germany’s most beautiful castles.

Bonus:
Rothenburg ob der Tauber – The best-preserved medieval town in Germany.
Lake Constance – Straddling Germany, Austria & Switzerland.
Wartburg Castle – Where Martin Luther translated the Bible

description:
Cameroon proudly celebrates its 65th anniversary of independence, marking over six decades of unity and cultural richness. Often dubbed “Africa in miniature,” Cameroon boasts an extraordinary array of landscapes—from golden beaches and dense rainforests to arid savannas and volcanic mountains .

The southern region is enveloped by lush equatorial rainforests, home to towering hardwoods like mahogany and ebony, as well as vibrant orchids and ferns . Moving northward, the terrain transitions into rolling highlands and expansive savannas, where wildlife such as elephants, giraffes, and antelopes roam freely . Along the coast, towns like Kribi offer pristine white-sand beaches and the unique spectacle of waterfalls cascading directly into the sea.

At the heart of this diverse nation lies Yaoundé, the capital city, nestled among seven verdant hills. Yaoundé is a vibrant hub of Cameroonian culture, blending historical significance with modern vitality. The city is home to several notable museums, including the National Museum, which showcases artifacts from all ten regions of Cameroon, and the Blackitude Museum, dedicated to preserving royal and traditional art . Additionally, the Musée des Peuples de la Forêt offers insights into the traditions of the forest-dwelling communities.

Cameroon's cultural tapestry is woven from over 250 ethnic groups, each contributing unique languages, music, and customs. This diversity is celebrated through vibrant festivals, traditional dances, and a rich culinary scene that reflects the nation's multifaceted heritage.

As Cameroon commemorates this significant milestone, it invites the world to explore its natural wonders and immerse themselves in its dynamic cultural landscape. The 65th anniversary of independence is not only a time for reflection but also an opportunity to experience the enduring spirit and unity of the Cameroonian people.

For those seeking cultural immersion, the country's rich tapestry includes ancient petroglyphs, historic Silk Road sites, and vibrant local traditions. Whether trekking through rugged canyons, riding horseback across open plains, or experiencing the haunting melodies of the Singing Dune, Kazakhstan invites travelers to discover its myriad adventures.

description:
The Jordan Trail is a remarkable 675-kilometer (420-mile) long-distance hiking route that traverses the entire length of Jordan, from the verdant hills of Um Qais in the north to the Red Sea port of Aqaba in the south. Established in 2015 by the Jordan Trail Association, this trail offers an immersive journey through the country's diverse landscapes, rich history, and vibrant culture.
Divided into eight distinct sections, the trail guides hikers through a variety of terrains, including rolling hills, rugged mountains, expansive deserts, and deep canyons. Notable natural landmarks along the route include the Dana Biosphere Reserve and the dramatic Wadi Mujib gorge. The trail also passes through over 75 towns and villages, providing opportunities to experience Jordanian hospitality and engage with local communities.
Historically, the Jordan Trail follows ancient trade routes once traversed by merchants and pilgrims. It connects several significant archaeological and cultural sites, including the UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Petra and Wadi Rum. Petra, known as the "Rose City," is renowned for its rock-cut architecture and historical significance as the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom. Wadi Rum, also called the "Valley of the Moon," is famous for its stunning desert landscapes and ancient petroglyphs.
Hiking the entire trail typically takes around 40 days, but many opt to explore shorter sections, such as the popular Dana to Petra segment, which offers a five-day trek through some of Jordan's most breathtaking scenery. The trail is best experienced in spring (March to May) or autumn (September to November) when the weather is most favorable.
The Jordan Trail not only showcases the country's natural beauty and historical treasures but also serves as a bridge connecting travelers to the heart of Jordan's cultural heritage.

Laos, a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, has become more accessible than ever with the inauguration of the Laos-China Railway. This 414-kilometer high-speed rail line, completed in December 2021, connects the capital city, Vientiane, to the northern border town of Boten, facilitating seamless travel into China's Yunnan province. The railway has significantly reduced travel times between major cities, such as the journey from Vientiane to Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, now taking less than three hours compared to previous road trips that could span up to 13 hours .

This enhanced connectivity has spurred a notable increase in tourism. In 2024, Laos welcomed over five million international visitors, contributing more than US$1 billion to its economy . The railway has made it easier for travelers to explore Laos's rich cultural heritage and stunning natural landscapes. Destinations like Luang Prabang, known for its well-preserved architecture and vibrant traditions, and Vang Vieng, famed for its karst mountains and riverine scenery, have become more accessible, encouraging sustainable tourism practices and cultural exchange.

Beyond tourism, the railway has bolstered trade and employment. As of late 2024, it had facilitated the transport of over 10 million tons of goods, valued at approximately $5.74 billion . The project has also created numerous job opportunities, with over 1,000 Lao employees working on the railway and more than 100,000 jobs generated in related sectors .

While the railway presents economic and social benefits, it also brings challenges, including concerns over national debt and environmental impacts. Nevertheless, the Laos-China Railway stands as a transformative development, opening new avenues for exploration and growth in this culturally rich and geographically diverse nation.

Trinidad & Tobago, a breathtaking twin-island nation in the southern Caribbean, is a destination that blends vibrant culture with unspoiled natural beauty. Most famously, Trinidad bursts to life each year with its world-renowned Carnival — a spectacular display of music, dance, and elaborate costumes. Tobago, the smaller sister island, offers serene white-sand beaches, coral reefs for snorkeling and diving, and a slower, more tranquil pace. Its turquoise waters and laid-back charm invite travelers to unwind and reconnect with nature.
Trinidad & Tobago is also a melting pot of cultures, reflected in its diverse cuisine, music, and festivals. From the rhythm of steelpan and soca to the aromas of curry, roti, and fresh seafood, every moment engages the senses.
Whether you seek the exhilaration of Carnival, the wonder of wildlife, or the richness of Caribbean culture, Trinidad & Tobago promises an unforgettable journey filled with heart, harmony, and discovery.

Nestled in the heart of Central Europe, Slovakia is a breathtaking destination that’s quickly gaining recognition for its unspoiled natural beauty and commitment to sustainable tourism. This compact country offers an array of outdoor adventures that cater to both thrill-seekers and nature lovers. Towering peaks in the High Tatras invite hikers to explore alpine trails, where glacial lakes shimmer beneath rugged mountain backdrops. For a unique underground experience, Slovakia is home to some of Europe’s most awe-inspiring ice caves, including the UNESCO-listed Dobšiná Ice Cave, where shimmering formations have formed over millennia.
Beyond the thrill of exploration, Slovakia is making strides in ecotourism and environmental restoration. National parks like Slovenský Raj (Slovak Paradise) and Pieniny protect rich biodiversity and fragile ecosystems, while offering eco-conscious trails, wooden ladders, and walkways that blend harmoniously with the landscape. The government and local communities are also investing in green initiatives—such as reforestation projects, protected wildlife zones, and sustainable farming—to ensure future generations can continue to enjoy the country's natural heritage.
Charming medieval towns like Banská Štiavnica and Levoča provide a historical counterpoint to Slovakia’s wild side, with cobbled streets, Gothic cathedrals, and preserved castles. Visitors can immerse themselves in folk traditions, taste organic Slovak cuisine, and support eco-lodges and rural homestays that promote responsible travel.
Whether trekking through dramatic gorges, kayaking along emerald rivers, or discovering ancient ruins, Slovakia offers an authentic European escape with a growing focus on environmental care. It’s a destination where adventure meets preservation, and where every traveler can play a role in protecting the planet.

Stretching along the southern belt of Nepal, the Terai region offers a profound contrast to the towering Himalayas to the north. This lush, fertile plain is more than just a geographical boundary—it's a living, breathing mosaic of biodiversity, ancient traditions, and spiritual significance. As you travel through its vast expanses, you’re greeted by golden fields of rice and mustard, thick sal forests, and a warm, welcoming culture shaped by centuries of coexistence with the land.
One of the Terai’s most sacred jewels is Lumbini, the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama—the Buddha. Here, pilgrims from across the world come to walk the peaceful paths of the Maya Devi Temple complex, meditate under the Bodhi trees, and visit serene monasteries representing Buddhist traditions from countries as far as Japan, Thailand, and Germany. The spiritual atmosphere in Lumbini is palpable, offering a quiet space for reflection and inner peace.
Beyond the spiritual, the Terai is home to stunning natural reserves such as Chitwan and Bardia National Parks, where you can embark on jungle safaris to glimpse rhinos, Bengal tigers, elephants, and countless bird species. Local Tharu villages provide an intimate look into the region’s indigenous heritage through traditional dances, handcrafted art, and mud-plastered homes.
Whether you’re exploring spiritual roots, seeking wildlife adventures, or absorbing the daily rhythms of rural life, the Terai invites you to slow down and connect deeply—with nature, with culture, and with yourself.

Its dramatic landscapes include smoldering volcanoes like Mount Yasur on Tanna Island—one of the world’s most accessible active volcanoes—where visitors can stand at the rim and witness fiery eruptions under the night sky.

Local Ni-Vanuatu communities welcome travelers with traditional dances, firewalking ceremonies, and storytelling passed down through generations. These experiences offer a glimpse into a way of life that has remained remarkably unchanged over time.
Whether you’re hiking across volcanic craters, swimming in pristine blue holes, or learning about ancient tribal customs, Vanuatu delivers a rich tapestry of adventure, authenticity, and natural beauty. Culturally, Paraguay boasts a unique blend of Indigenous Guaraní and Spanish influences. This fusion is evident in the country’s music, cuisine, and the widely spoken Guaraní language, which remains a vital part of everyday life.

description:

 Welcome to the enchanting province of Nan, Thailand, where every turn reveals a breathtaking surprise. Join us on a journey through stunning landscapes of these beautiful mountains.  

Nestled in the heart of Northern Thailand, Nan Province boasts some of the most awe-inspiring roads you'll ever encounter. Picture yourself cruising along twisty and winding paths, surrounded by lush greenery, as the gentle breeze caresses your face.

 And what better way to take in the beauty of Nan than from a cozy coffee shop with a panoramic view at our first stop of the journey. Sip on your favorite brew as you gaze out onto the rolling hills, admiring the majestic landscape that stretches as far as the eye can see. It's a tranquil oasis that will rejuvenate your soul.

Next stop the famous Street Number 3 road, and you will understand the name as soon as you see the road.  

Ten travel back in time and witness the legacy of Nan's 800-year-old salt mines. These historical treasures have been a cornerstone of the province's economy for centuries. As you explore the well-preserved remnants of this ancient industry, you'll gain a deeper appreciation for the resilience and ingenuity of the local people.

Finally a view from the awe inspiring 1715 Viewpoint on top of the mountain.  Sure to take your breath away.  

Day one of our Nan visit and already we are smitten.  Take a trip with us to this beautiful province

description:

Join us on our journey today into Singapore's Cultural Gems, the vibrant parts of the city that are a fun and must visit.  

We start in Chinatown where history and modernity blend seemlessly where we  wander thru the bustling streets lined with traditional shophouses, and newer vendors all doing their best to sell us something nice.  We meet a tailor whose been there for 35 years.

Explore the bustling markets of Serangoon Road where you can find everything from fresh flowers to amazing jewelry and delicious Indian snacks.

Stroll along the streets adorned with colorful textiles and unique boutiques.  Its also a haven for street art and trendy cafes and fantastic restaurants. description:
Our last day in Hanoi, and a busy, fun one it was. We started by heading to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum which serves as the resting place of the Vietnamese revolutionary leader and President Ho Chi Minh. Next we visit the famous (infamous) Hanoi Hilton  (Hoa Lo Prison) where Senator McCain and many other American POW's were incarcerated during the Vietnam war. Next was a Banh Mi sandwich for lunch, and a visit to a beautiful temple that we lucked into finding. And it really is beautiful. Back to the Train Market for another close train pass by, and crazy traffic all around the area where you must be on your toes to keep from getting run over. Dinner followed, followed by a walk around beautiful Old Quarter Hanoi at night and a rooftop nightcap. The next day we went back to St Joseph Church and were able to go in and show you how beautiful it is.

title: We Found Devastating Termite Damage. Will Tikkie's Mom's House Survive?
tags: #ThailandLife|#IssanThailand|#TermiteProblem|#ThaiHouseTour|#EarthQuakeThailand|#BangkokCondo|#KalasinTrip|#ThaiCulture|#BangkokandBeyond|#TikkieandJerry|#RuralLivingThailand|#TermitesinThailand|#DinosaurBridgeThailand|#ThepsudaBridge
description:
Our three--day trip to Kalasin, Thailand started off peaceful--but on Day 3 things took a dramatic turn.

After enjoying a delicious Western-style breakfast at a just discovered restaurant in Kalasin City, we headed to Makro to buy supplies for mom, dad and grandma. On the way back we took a short detour to check out giant dinosaur statues near Thepsuda Bridge which crosses over a beautiful dam/lake which will be flooded with party goers soon for Songkran.

Then it was time to head to Tikkie's family home--and that's when the real surprise hit. We inspected the upper wooden floor of the house and discovered extensive termite damage. Just as we were discussing what to do next, we got news of an earthquake in Myanmar that was felt all the way in Bangkok!

The rest of the day was filled with questions: Should we stay overnight in Khon Kaen? Drive the rental car back to Bangkok? If we fly home will we be able to get back to the condo from the airport?

We finally made it back to Bangkok and discovered cracks in our condo walls and ceilings from the quake. It was a wild end to what started as a beautiful rural getaway.

Join us as we explore life in rural Thailand, deal with unexpected natural disasters, and share an authentic slice of life in Kalasin and beyond.

title: Peaceful Songkran in Bangkok | Friends, Food & Local Life | It Doesn't Always Have to be Crazy Here
tags: #Songkran2025|#BangkokThailandCelebrations|#ThaiNewYear|#bangkokandBeyond|#TikkieandJerry|#TawandangGermanBrewery|#GordonRamsaysBreadStreet|#Ohkajhu|#CafeAmazonm#BangkokVlog|#ExpatLifeThailand|#BrangkokStreetFood|#MeetupBangkok
description:
It's Thai New Year -- known as Songkran -- a tie when Bangkok usually turns into the biggest water fight in the world, and lots of fun! But this year, instead of getting soaked, we enjoyed a peaceful side of the city, spending quality time with friends and savoring great food. 

Our Songkran week started with lunch at Gordon Ramsay's Bread Street Kitchen in Emsphere, followed by a festive dinner at Tawandang German Brewery with our friend Ren and his family visiting from Peru. Along the way we got to enjoy some fun Songkran happenings in our neighborhood.

The next day we kept it local -- enjoying breakfast pancakes from our favorite local street food vendor and coffee at Cafe' Amazon on our soi. After that I joined my weekly Meetup group, and caught up for lunch with Dave, Vance and our good friend Jim, just in from the US. 

That evening Tikkie and I shared a cozy dinner at one of our favorite EmQuartier restaurants where the portions are so huge we took home enough food for two more meals. 

To wrap up the Songkron week, we strolled around Sukhumvit's Phrom Phong area, capturing the street scenes and showing what the city looks like during the Thai New Year without the usual splashy chaos.

If you want to see a quieter, more local side of Bangkok during Songkran - this video is for you.

title: 🇮🇹 Rome Solo Mission | Tax ID, U.S. Embassy & Michelangelo’s Church | Italy Vlog Ep. 2

description:
In Episode 2 of our Rome and Mediterranean Cruise travel series, Jerry spends a busy Thursday solo in Rome, balancing Italian bureaucracy with historic discovery and a well-earned lunch.

The day begins with a visit to the Italian tax office, where Jerry takes the first step toward his dream of Italian dual citizenship by applying for a codice fiscale (Italian tax ID). From there, he enjoys a relaxing late lunch at a local Roman café, soaking in the atmosphere before heading to the U.S. Embassy in Rome to notarize a power of attorney—a process that goes smoothly, but with one unexpected twist: the document must be legalized at a separate office the next day (Friday), or it won’t be valid in Italy. Luckily, that timing works out, as Tikkie arrives just in time to join the next day’s adventure.

Between errands, Jerry explores the area near the embassy and steps inside the breathtaking Basilica of Santa Maria degli Angeli e dei Martiri, a former Roman bath transformed into a church by Michelangelo.

We captured some of our favorite video and photos there, especially of the incredible Caravaggio paintings, which are displayed right inside the cathedral and absolutely lived up to the legend.

Come along with us as we stroll through two of Malta’s most breathtaking cities, take in the art, the light, the architecture—and the joy of simply being there together.

title: “Kotor, Montenegro 🇲🇪 – The Most Beautiful Walled City You’ve Never Heard Of”
tags: Tikkie and Jerry|Bangkok and Beyond|Kotor Montenegro|Montenegro cruise port|Venetian history|walled cities Europe|Adriatic Sea|Montenegro travel vlog|Balkan travel|cruise vlog Montenegro|Princess Cruises Mediterranean|Kotor old town|fjord cruise|European travel series|stunning views Montenegro
description:
#KotorMontenegro #HiddenGemsOfEurope #TikkieAndJerry
Tucked deep within the Adriatic fjords lies a place that stunned us — the walled city of Kotor, Montenegro. With its medieval fortifications, Venetian alleys, and jaw-dropping mountain backdrop, Kotor might just be the most beautiful city you’ve never heard of.

🌊 The video begins with a serene cruise through the Bay of Kotor, a fjord-like inlet often called one of Europe’s best-kept secrets. As our ship glides into port, we’re greeted by fortified walls, medieval stone towers, and postcard-perfect views.

🏛️ Once ashore, we wander through Kotor’s UNESCO-listed Old Town, where 400 years of Venetian influence come to life in narrow alleys, Romanesque churches, and colorful flower boxes spilling from rustic stone windows. With Tikkie soaking in the beauty and Jerry capturing every moment, this walk through Kotor feels like traveling back in time.

🚤 After exploring the streets, we return to the ship and close the video with a final 5 minutes of sailing out through the fjord — a quiet, cinematic goodbye to one of the most beautiful places we've ever seen.

📸 This video is filled with unforgettable sights, heartfelt moments, and a deep appreciation for Kotor’s timeless beauty. Whether you’ve been here or are dreaming of going, we hope this episode leaves you inspired.

👇 Let us know in the comments — have you ever been to Kotor? Would you like to go?

Looking for Bangkok’s hidden shopping gem where only locals shop? 🛍️

Join Tikkie and Jerry as we head from our neighborhood café (after a morning neighborhood walk), to Union Mall Bangkok, a trendy local shopping center where Thais shop for fashion at real Thai prices.

This is not a tourist mall — Union Mall is where locals shop, and the vibe is stylish, youthful, and affordable. From women’s fashion to men’s clothes, every floor has something unique, and prices are already low so there’s no need to haggle (though you might get 20–40 baht off).

If you want authentic Bangkok shopping — trendy clothes, Thai prices, and a mall most tourists don’t even know exists — Union Mall is a must-visit.

description:

We drove up into the misty mountains of Phetchabun to visit what many call the most beautiful temple in Thailand — Wat Phra That Phasorn Kaew (วัดพระธาตุผาซ่อนแก้ว). Perched high in the clouds, this dazzling mountaintop sanctuary feels almost otherworldly. Five serene Buddhas sit in perfect alignment, surrounded by lotus-petal mosaics and golden arches that shimmer in the mountain light.

In this episode, we keep things simple — just a quiet walk, a bit of history, and time to take in the breathtaking scenery of Khao Kho, one of Thailand’s most stunning regions. Whether you come for the views, the architecture, or the peaceful energy, it’s easy to see why many travelers consider this Thailand’s most beautiful wat.

What makes this temple so special:
Perched on a mountain near Khao Kho, about 5–6 hours from Bangkok.
Famous for its five seated Buddhas and intricate mosaic-tile design that glitters in sunlight and mist.
Holds a sacred relic of a revered monk, adding deep spiritual meaning to its beauty.

Offers panoramic views, cool air, and tranquility rarely found elsewhere.

If you enjoyed this, please like and subscribe — it really helps our small channel keep exploring Thailand’s most beautiful places.

Gear & Credits: Filmed by Tikkie & Jerry • Bangkok & Beyond
Music: YouTube Audio Library

Travel notes (quick tips):

Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered).

Visit early or on weekdays for the best light and fewer crowds.

Weather changes quickly — clouds and mist make it even more magical.

Today I’m in Ari, one of my favorite neighborhoods in Bangkok, exploring one of the city’s most unusual and thought-provoking places: the Kid Mai Death Awareness Café. This café is part museum, part social experiment, and part immersive art installation designed to help people reflect on life, death, and the choices we make along the way.

I met up with friends Vance, Robert, and Noi, and together we walked through the full experience — the organ jars, the anatomical displays, the “final bed,” the pitch-black coffin reflection room, and even the unusual “birth tunnel.” Kid Mai goes far beyond being a café; it’s a surreal, philosophical, slightly bizarre journey through the cycle of life.

If you’re looking for hidden gems in Bangkok, unique experiences, or just something completely different to do in Bangkok, this place is unforgettable. Join me for a full walkthrough inside the Death Café and a look at what makes Ari one of the most interesting neighborhoods in the city.

#TokyoAtNight #ShibuyaCrossing #shinjuku 
Tokyo comes alive at night — and this was the perfect introduction.
From the iconic Shibuya Crossing to an unforgettable Shinjuku food tour, this night was pure energy.

Day 1, Part 2 of our Tokyo adventure — and this is where the city really starts to glow.

My friend Gene and I begin underground as an express train flies past us, then emerge into the organized chaos of Shibuya Crossing, one of the most famous intersections in the world. We walk with the crowd, soak in the atmosphere, and watch as everyone around us captures the moment — just like we are.

From there, we head up to Starbucks overlooking the crossing for coffee, hot chocolate, and a perfect bird’s-eye view of Shibuya in motion. After crossing again (because you have to), we make our way toward Shinjuku as night falls and the city transforms.

The evening continues with a guided Shinjuku food tour led by Sabina, where we visit four different restaurants and try 12–14 incredible dishes — including the best pork cutlet I’ve ever had. Along the way, we walk through the red-light district, take in the neon glow, pass Godzilla watching over the streets, and spot the famous 3D cat lighting up the night sky.

Tokyo is colorful, exciting, magnetic — and even if you’re not a “city person,” this is a city you feel.
I love Japan. I love Tokyo. And I hope this video makes you want to experience it for yourself.

Bangkok has a side almost nobody ever sees.
In this video, we explore Bangkok’s secret canals and backstreets by small boat through Old Lumphu (Baan Lamphu) Village, just minutes from the Grand Palace and Chinatown.

These historic canals were once used by Thai kings to travel between temples — today they’re quiet, underused, and full of hidden local life.

We start at the Lumphu Museum and then take small boats deep into Bangkok’s back canals, passing under low bridges and through narrow waterways most visitors never experience.

Along the way, we explore:
Historic khlongs once used by royalty
Hidden canal-side sois and pedestrian bridges
A peaceful two-hour mix of boat rides and walking
A stop at AMA Hostel, a beautifully restored Chinese-style building
The neighborhood around Zafran Indian Restaurant, a personal favorite

This was just the three amigos — Robert, Vance, and me — wandering through one of Bangkok’s most overlooked neighborhoods.

description:
#Syros #Greece #GreekIslands

Join us as we explore the beautiful island of Syros, Greece 🇬🇷

On this 22-minute walking tour, Tikkie and I wander through the charming streets of Ermoupoli, the capital of the Cyclades. Along the way, we'll discover colorful architecture, waterfront promenades, scenic harbor views, local neighborhoods, and some of the most beautiful city views we found during our Greek island cruise.

Syros is unlike many of the other Greek islands. While famous destinations such as Mykonos and Santorini are known primarily for tourism, Syros has long served as the administrative and cultural capital of the Cyclades. Its elegant architecture, grand public buildings, and beautiful harbor reflect a rich maritime history that helped make Ermoupoli one of Greece's most important commercial centers during the 19th century. Today, visitors can still see that fascinating blend of history, culture, and island charm throughout the city.

One of the highlights of our visit was touring the historic Church of the Dormition of the Virgin. The beautiful interior, remarkable artwork, and peaceful atmosphere made it one of the most memorable churches we visited in Greece. Built in the early 19th century, the church remains one of Syros' most important landmarks and offers visitors a glimpse into the island's rich religious and cultural heritage.

Syros offers a different side of Greece—beautiful waterfront scenery, authentic local character, impressive architecture, fascinating history, and a relaxed atmosphere that invites you to slow down and enjoy the experience.

We hope you'll come along and explore this beautiful Greek island together with us.

title: Volleyball In Korea -
Gyeongju - The Golden City of South Korea, the History in Gyeongju
description:
Save this video and locations for your next Gyeongju Trip

1. Luge World  

루지 is a non-powered cart-type amusement ride that uses gravity without a special power device and is an all-season experience sport that can be enjoyed dynamically by anyone of any age and gender by easily adjusting direction and braking through terrain and slopes.

Gyeongju Luge World has two courses, the 1.6km Hwarang Course and the 1.4km Cheonma Course, which are 3km long and sloped, making them great for riding at speed.

When you come down from the luge cart, take in the beautiful view of Gyeongju Bomun Gate at a glance. With Gyeongju Luge World, the pleasure of traveling to Gyeongju is doubled.

Address: 6, Cheonbuknam-ro, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do 
Tel: 1833-2923
Operating Time: 9:20 - 20:00

2. Woljeonggyo Bridge

The Iljeonggyo and Woljeonggyo Bridges are presumed to be the bridges referred to in a passage of Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms) that reads: “In the second moth of the nineteenth year of King Gyeongdeok’s reign, two bridges, Chunyang and Woljeong, were built over the Muncheon stream on the south side of the palace.” Over time, the name “Woljeong” came to be written as “月精” instead of “月淨,” and the name “Chunyanggyo” was replaced by “Iljeonggyo,” “Hyobulhyogyo” or “Chilseonggyo.” The names appear to have eventually become settled as Iljeonggyo and Woljeonggyo, symbolizing the spirit of the sun and the spirit of the moon, respectively. As for the names “Hyobulhyogyo” and “Chilseonggyo,” they seemed to have emerged during the Joseon period, from folk legends that became associated with the Iljeonggyo Bridge.

Address: 경상북도 경주시 교동 48
Contact number: 054-779-6138
Operating Hours: Open from 9:00 am

3. Shilla-Style Hanbok Rental

Yeogi Hanbok has various hanbok designs for customers to try and wear while exploring different parts of woljeonggyo and the nearby hanok village. The hanbok rental shop has distinct Shill style hanboks that can be worn until 19:00 

Address: 150-6 Hwangnam-dong Gyeongju-si Gyeongsangbuk-do
Contact number 0507-1321-5653
Operating Hour - Open from 11:00 - 19:00

4. Wonder Space

This 5 floor attraction in Gyeongju has  a lot of experiences you can try!
a. 1st floor has the parking lot and entrance to the Wonder Space
b. 2nd floor has the arcade area where you can play different arcade games! 
c. 3rd floor has the noodle factory where you can eat and try different games related to noodles - noodle claw machine
d. 4th floor is the Raiders Arena zone. I wanted to try this floor but we lacked time for this event so I had to just watch other people play and enjoy their laser tag game
e. 5th floor has the photo zones. I enjoyed these photo areas as I can see different locations just by going around the 5th floor.


5. Jungdo Tower

This tower is modeled and inspired from the ancient nine-story wooden pagoda of Hwangnyongsa Temple built during Shilla period.

Address: Jungdo Tower (중도타워), Gyeongju, South Korea Landscape

title: Suwon - Two Cities in one day! Starfield Library, Railroad Museum and more
tags: uiwang|suwon|korea|korea trip|korea itinerary|suwon itinerary|railbike|suwon fortress
description:
Have you been it Uiwang and Suwon City? These places are just outside Seoul and can easily be accessed through the Korean subway! 

On September 28, 2024, I decided to visit one of the key cities in South Korea and experience the tourist life in Suwon City. For this trip, I made a quick visit to Uiwang Station and explored the different attractions in the area - Uiwang Railroad Museum, Railbike, and the Wangsong Lake Park. After this, I visited Starfield Suwon to see the new library that has been the talk of the town with its size and aesthetics.

After this, I visited the Hwaseong Fortress and walked around the area to see the life in Suwon at night!

The next day, I explored the Suwon Hwaseong Fortress and learned about the construction and culture in Suwon City. To cap my day, I rode the Flying Suwon and gazed at the city view from 200 meters above. The experience in Hwaseong will not be complete without the Hanbok experience while exploring the Temporary Place in Hwaseong, where the majority of historical Korean dramas were filmed.

tags: Google Earth Studio|Google|Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro|Brazil|Google Map|Christ the redeemer|Rio de Janeiro|Visit Brazil|Best places in Brazil|Brazil travel guide|jesus cristo|rio brazil
description:
Vincentian priest Pedro Maria Boss first suggested placing a Christian monument on Mount Corcovado in the mid-1850s to honor Princess Isabel, regent of Brazil and the daughter of Emperor Pedro II, but the project was not approved. In 1889, the country became a republic, and owing to the separation of church and state the proposed statute was dismissed.

The Catholic Circle of Rio made a second proposal for a landmark statue on the mountain in 1920.[9] The group organized an event called Semana do Monumento ("Monument Week") to attract donations and collect signatures to support the building of the statue. The organization was motivated by what they perceived as "Godlessness" in society. The donations came mostly from Brazilian Catholics. The designs considered for the "Statue of the Christ" included a representation of the Christian cross, a statue of Jesus with a globe in his hands, and a pedestal symbolizing the world. The statue of Christ the Redeemer with open arms, a symbol of peace, was chosen.

title: Tokyo Tower is a telecommunications and observation tower in Tokyo , Japan
tags: Google Earth Studio|Google|Google Map|Tokyo Skytree is a broadcasting and observation tower in Sumida|Tokyo|Tokyo Skytree|Sumida city|Visit Japan|Tallest building in Japan|Visit Tokyo|Japanese tallest structure|tallest structure in Japan|Tokyo Tower|japan travel guide|japan travel tips|tokyo city|tokyo travel|tokyo travel guide
description:
Tokyo Tower is a telecommunications and observation tower located in the Shiba Park area of ​​Minato, Tokyo, Japan.​​ At 332.9 m high, it is the second tallest structure in Japan. It is a lattice tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower that is painted white and international orange to comply with air safety regulations .

Built in 1958, its main sources of income are tourism and antenna rental. More than 150 million people have visited the tower since its inauguration. FootTown, a four-story building located just below the tower, houses museums, restaurants and shops. From there, visitors can also access the two viewpoints: the main viewpoint ( Main Deck ), which has two floors and is 150 m high; and the smaller Top Deck, which is located at a height of 249.6 m. 

The tower acts as a support structure for a telecommunications antenna. Initially intended for television broadcasting, radio antennas were also installed in 1961, but currently, the tower broadcasts signals from Japanese television networks such as NHK , TBS and Fuji TV . After the transition to digital television in Japan, planned for July 2011, the height of the Tokyo Tower was not sufficient to support a complete broadcast of digital terrestrial television to the area, so on February 29, 2012 it was built a taller digital broadcasting tower, called Tokyo Skytree.

The Wawel Royal Castle (Polish pronunciation:; Zamek Królewski na Wawelu) and the Wawel Hill on which it sits constitute the most historically and culturally significant site in Poland. A fortified residency on the Vistula River in Kraków, it was established on the orders of King Casimir III the Great and enlarged over the centuries into several structures around an Italian-styled courtyard. It represents nearly all European architectural styles of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque periods.

The castle is part of a fortified architectural complex erected atop a limestone outcrop on the left bank of the Vistula River, at an altitude of 228 meters above sea level. The complex consists of numerous buildings of great historical and national importance, including the Wawel Cathedral where Polish monarchs were crowned and buried. Some of Wawel's oldest stone buildings can be traced back to 970 AD, in addition to the earliest examples of Romanesque and Gothic architecture in Poland.[5][6] The current castle was built in the 14th century and expanded over the next hundreds of years. In 1978 Wawel was declared the first World Heritage Site as part of the Historic Centre of Kraków.

tags: Google Earth Studio|Google|Google Map|Windsor Castle|Castles in England|List of castles in the world|Most beautiful castle in the world|Best royal castle|Allington Castle|in England|Poland|Kraków|Best places in Poland|Visit Poland|Castle in Poland|Malbork Castle|Malbork City|Malbork Castle in Poland
description:
The Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork, commonly known as Malbork Castle (Polish: Zamek w Malborku; German: Ordensburg Marienburg), is a 13th-century castle complex located in the town of Malbork, Poland. It is the largest castle in the world measured by land area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

It was originally constructed by the Teutonic Order, a German Catholic religious order of crusaders, in the form of an Ordensburg fortress and named Marienburg in honour of Mary, mother of Jesus. In 1457, during the Thirteen Years' War, the castle was sold by Bohemian mercenaries to King Casimir IV of Poland in lieu of indemnities. It then served as one of several Polish royal residences and the seat of Polish offices and institutions, interrupted by several years of Swedish occupation, fulfilling this function until the First Partition of Poland in 1772. From then on, the castle was under German rule for over 170 years until 1945, albeit largely falling into disrepair as military technological advances rendered the castle a mere historical point of interest.

The construction period is a point of debate, but most historians generally accept the 132 years between 1274 and 1406 as the construction time. The castle is a classic example of a medieval fortress and, upon its completion in 1406, was the world's largest brick castle.

UNESCO designated the "Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork" and the Malbork Castle Museum a World Heritage Site in December 1997. It is one of two World Heritage Sites in the region (north-central Poland), together with the "Medieval Town of Toruń", which was founded in 1231.

Königstein Fortress (German: Festung Königstein), the "Saxon Bastille", is a hilltop fortress near Dresden, in Saxon Switzerland, Germany, above the town of Königstein on the left bank of the River Elbe. It is one of the largest hilltop fortifications in Europe and sits atop the table hill of the same name.

The 9.5-hectare (23-acre) rock plateau rises 240 metres (790 ft) above the Elbe and has over 50 buildings, some over 400 years old, that bear witness to the military and civilian life in the fortress. The rampart run of the fortress is 1,800 metres (5,900 ft) long with walls up to 42 metres (138 ft) high and steep sandstone faces. In the centre of the site is a 152.5-metre-deep (500 ft 4 in) well, which is the deepest in Saxony and second-deepest well in Europe.

The fortress, which for centuries was used as a state prison, is still intact and is now one of Saxony's foremost tourist attractions, with 700,000 visitors per year.

description:
Arundel Castle is a restored and remodeled medieval castle in Arundel, West Sussex, England. It was established by Roger de Montgomery in the 11th century. The castle was damaged in the English Civil War and then restored in the 18th and early 19th centuries by Charles Howard, 11th Duke of Norfolk. Further restoration and embellishment were undertaken in the 1890s by Charles Alban Buckler for the 15th Duke.

Since the 11th century, the castle has been the seat of the Earls of Arundel and the Dukes of Norfolk. It is a Grade I listed building.

History
The original structure was a motte-and-bailey castle. Roger de Montgomery was declared the first Earl of Arundel as the King granted him the property as part of a much larger package of hundreds of manors. Roger, who was a cousin of William the Conqueror, had stayed in Normandy to keep the peace there while William was away in England. He was rewarded for his loyalty with extensive lands in the Welsh Marches and across the country, together with one-fifth of Sussex (Arundel Rape). He began work on Arundel Castle in around 1067.

Between 1101 and 1102 the castle was besieged by the forces of Henry I after its holder Robert of Bellême rebelled.[5] The siege ended with the castle surrendering to the king.  The castle then passed to Adeliza of Louvain (who had previously been married to Henry I) and her husband William d'Aubigny. Empress Matilda stayed in the castle, in 1139.[4] It then passed down the d'Aubigny line until the death of Hugh d'Aubigny, 5th Earl of Arundel in 1243.[4] John Fitzalan then inherited jure matris the castle and honor of Arundel, by which, according to Henry VI's "admission" of 1433, he was later retrospectively held to have become de jure Earl of Arundel.

description:
Kenilworth Castle is a castle in the town of Kenilworth in Warwickshire, England, managed by English Heritage; much of it is still in ruins. The castle was founded during the Norman conquest of England; with development through to the Tudor period. It has been described by the architectural historian Anthony Emery as "the finest surviving example of a semi-royal palace of the later middle ages, significant for its scale, form and quality of workmanship".

Kenilworth played an important historical role: it was the subject of the six-month-long siege of Kenilworth in 1266, thought to be the longest siege in Medieval English history, and formed a base for Lancastrian operations in the Wars of the Roses. Kenilworth was the scene of the removal of Edward II from the English throne, the perceived French insult to Henry V in 1414 of a gift of tennis balls (said by John Strecche to have prompted the campaign that led to the Battle of Agincourt), and the Earl of Leicester's lavish reception of Elizabeth I in 1575. It has been described as "one of two major castles in Britain which may be classified as water-castles or lake-fortresses.

The castle was built over several centuries. Founded in the 1120s around a powerful Norman great tower, the castle was significantly enlarged by King John at the beginning of the 13th century. Huge water defenses were created by damming the local streams, and the resulting fortifications proved able to withstand assaults by land and water in 1266. John of Gaunt spent lavishly in the late 14th century, turning the medieval castle into a palace fortress designed in the latest perpendicular style. The Earl of Leicester then expanded the castle during his tenure in the 16th century, constructing new Tudor buildings and exploiting the medieval heritage of Kenilworth to produce a fashionable Renaissance palace.

description:
York Castle is a fortified complex in the city of York, England. It consists of a sequence of castles, prisons, law courts, and other buildings, which were built over the last nine centuries on the south side of the River Foss. The now ruined keep of the medieval Norman castle is commonly referred to as Clifford's Tower. Built originally on the orders of William I to dominate the former Viking city of Jórvík, the castle suffered a tumultuous early history before developing into a major fortification with extensive water defenses. After a major explosion in 1684 rendered the remaining military defenses uninhabitable, York Castle continued to be used as a jail and prison until 1929.

The first motte and bailey castle on the site was built in 1068 following the Norman conquest of York. After the destruction of the castle by rebels and a Viking army in 1069, York Castle was rebuilt and reinforced with extensive water defenses, including a moat and an artificial lake. York Castle formed an important royal fortification in the north of England.

In 1190, 150 local Jews were murdered in a pogrom in the timber castle keep; most of them died by suicide in order not to fall into the hands of the mob. Henry III rebuilt the castle in stone in the middle of the 13th century, creating a keep with a unique quatrefoil design, supported by an outer bailey wall and a substantial gatehouse. During the Scottish wars between 1298 and 1338, York Castle was frequently used as the center of royal administration across England, as well as an important military base of operations.

Lincoln Castle is a major medieval castle constructed in Lincoln, England, during the late 11th century by William the Conqueror on the site of a pre-existing Roman fortress. Lincoln Castle remained in use as a prison and court into modern times and is one of the better-preserved castles in England; the Crown Courts continue to this day. It is open to the public most days of the week and possible to walk around the walls from which there are views of the castle complex, cathedral, the city, and surrounding countryside. Lumley Castle is a 14th-century quadrangular castle at Chester-le-Street in the North of England, near the city of Durham, and a property of the Earl of Scarbrough. It is a Grade I listed building. It is currently a hotel.
It is named after its original creator, Sir Ralph Lumley, who converted his family manor house into a castle in 1389 after returning from wars in Scotland. However, after being implicated in a plot to overthrow Henry IV, he was imprisoned and ultimately executed, forfeiting his lands to the Earl of Somerset. In 1421 the ownership of the castle reverted to Sir Ralph Lumley's grandson, Thomas.

During the time of John Lumley, 1st Baron Lumley, he altered the windows of the castle to let more light in, installed a new fireplace in the great hall along with a lavabo of black and white marble, adorned by a pelican, which is the crest of the Lumley coat of the arms. On the accession of James VI and I as King of England in 1603, he journeyed from Edinburgh to London to take his new throne. On 13 April, en route from Newcastle upon Tyne to Durham, he stopped briefly at the castle as a guest of Lord Lumley. The King James Suite hotel room commemorates this connection with the king. However, the suite was previously the chapel; the king did not stay at Lumley overnight, instead traveling later that day and staying at Durham Castle.

description:
The Castle, Newcastle, or Newcastle Castle is a medieval fortification in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, built on the site of the fortress that gave the City of Newcastle its name. The most prominent remaining structures on the site are the Castle Keep (the castle's main fortified stone tower, pictured below right), and the Black Gate, its fortified gatehouse.

Use of the site for defensive purposes dates from Roman times, when it housed a fort and settlement called Pons Aelius (meaning 'bridge of (Publius) Aelius (Hadrianus)' - the Roman emperor Hadrian), guarding a bridge over the River Tyne. Robert Curthose, eldest son of William the Conqueror, in 1080 built a wooden motte and bailey-style castle on the site of the Roman fort. Curthose built this 'New Castle upon Tyne' after he returned south from a campaign against Malcolm III of Scotland. Henry II built the stone Castle Keep between 1172 and 1177 on the site of Curthose's castle. Henry III added the Black Gate between 1247 and 1250. Nothing remains above the ground of the Roman fort or the original motte and bailey castle. The Keep is a Grade I listed building and a Scheduled Ancient Monument.

The Castle Keep and Black Gate pre-date the construction of the Newcastle town wall, construction of which started around 1265, and did not include it. The site of the keep is in the center of Newcastle and lies to the east of Newcastle station. The 75-foot (23 m) gap between the keep and the gatehouse is almost entirely filled by the railway viaduct that carries the East Coast Main Line from Newcastle to Scotland.

The Keep and Black Gate are now managed by the Old Newcastle Project under the Heart of the City Partnership as one combined visitor attraction, "Newcastle Castle".

description:
The London Eye, or the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom, with over three million visitors annually. It has made many appearances in popular culture.

The structure is 135 metres (443 ft) tall, and the wheel has a diameter of 120 metres (394 ft). When it opened to the public in 2000, it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel. Its height was surpassed by the 160 metres (525 ft) Star of Nanchang in 2006, the 165 metres (541 ft) Singapore Flyer in 2008, the 167 metres (548 ft) High Roller (Las Vegas) in 2014, and the 250 metres (820 ft) Ain Dubai in 2021. Supported by an A-frame on one side only, unlike these taller examples, the Eye is described by its operators as "the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel". The Eye offered the highest public viewing point in London until it was superseded by the 245-metre-high (804 ft) observation deck on the 72nd floor of The Shard in early 2013.

The London Eye adjoins the western end of Jubilee Gardens (previously the site of the former Dome of Discovery), on the South Bank of the River Thames between Westminster Bridge and Hungerford Bridge beside County Hall, in the London Borough of Lambeth. The nearest tube station is Waterloo.

description:
The Palace of Versailles French: château de Versailles is a former royal residence commissioned by King Louis XIV located in Versailles, about 19 kilometers (12 mi) west of Paris, France.

The palace is owned by the government of France and since 1995 has been managed, under the direction of the French Ministry of Culture, by the Public Establishment of the Palace, Museum, and National Estate of Versailles. About 15,000,000 people visit the palace, park, or gardens of Versailles every year, making it one of the most popular tourist attractions in the world.

Louis XIII built a simple hunting lodge on the site of the Palace of Versailles in 1623. With his death came Louis XIV who expanded the château into the beginnings of a palace that went through several changes and phases from 1661 to 1715. It was a favorite residence for both kings and in 1682, Louis XIV moved the seat of his court and government to Versailles, making the palace the de facto capital of France. This state of affairs was continued by Kings Louis XV and Louis XVI, who primarily made interior alterations to the palace, but in 1789 the royal family and capital of France returned to Paris. For the rest of the French Revolution, the Palace of Versailles was largely abandoned and emptied of its contents, and the population of the surrounding city plummeted.

The Château de Chambord (French pronunciation in Chambord, Centre-Val de Loire, France, is one of the most recognizable châteaux in the world because of its very distinctive French Renaissance architecture, which blends traditional French medieval forms with classical Renaissance structures. The building was constructed by the king of France, Francis I.

Chambord is the largest château in the Loire Valley; it was built to serve as a hunting lodge for Francis I, who maintained his royal residences at the Château de Blois and Amboise. The original design of the château is attributed to the Tuscan architect Domenico da Cortona; Leonardo da Vinci may have also influenced the design.

Chambord was altered considerably during the 28 years of its construction (1519–1547), during which it was overseen on-site by Pierre Neveu. With the château nearing completion, Francis showed off his enormous symbol of wealth and power by hosting his old archrival, Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, at Chambord.

description:
Craigmillar Castle is a ruined medieval castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It is three miles (4.8 km) southeast of the city center, on a low hill to the south of the modern suburb of Craigmillar. The Preston family of Craigmillar, the local feudal barons, began building the castle in the late 14th century and building works continued through the 15th and 16th centuries. In 1660, the castle was sold to Sir John Gilmour, Lord President of the Court of Session, who breathed new life into the aging castle. The Gilmours left Craigmillar in the 18th century for a more modern residence, nearby Inch House, and the castle fell into ruin. It is now in the care of Historic Environment Scotland as a scheduled monument and is open to the public.

Craigmillar Castle is best known for its association with Mary, Queen of Scots. Following an illness after the birth of her son, the future James VI, Mary arrived at Craigmillar on 20 November 1566 to convalesce. Before she left on 7 December 1566, a pact known as the "Craigmillar Bond" was made, with or without her knowledge, to dispose of her husband Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley.

description:
Thun Castle (German: Schloss Thun) is a castle in the city of Thun, in the Swiss canton of Bern. It was built in the 12th century, today houses the Thun Castle museum and is a Swiss heritage site of national significance.

History
During the Early Middle Ages, there was a small fort and church on the top of the castle hill. The castle was built between 1180 and 1190 by Duke Berthold V of Zähringen, who constructed the still-preserved keep to the level of the Knights' Hall (German: Rittersaal). The 14 m tall Knights' Hall was built as the centerpiece of a monument to Zähringen power. However, the family never lived in the castle, preferring Burgdorf Castle. In 1218 it was inherited by the House of Kyburg, who built the upper levels above the Zähringen castle. A quarrel over who would rule the southern Kyburg lands led, in 1322, to Eberhard II von Kyburg murdering his brother Hartmann II at the castle. To protect his newly acquired land from the Habsburgs Eberhard II then sold them to Bern and was promptly given them back as a fief. The Kyburgs ruled over the region for nearly two centuries until a failed raid by Rudolf II on Solothurn, in 1382, started the Burgdorferkrieg (also Kyburgerkrieg). After several decisive Bernese victories the Kyburgs were forced to concede an unfavorable peace. In 1384 Bern bought Thun and Burgdorf, the most important cities of the Kyburg lands. The castle came under Bernese control and became the seat of their local administration.

The current structure is the third church building to stand at this site. The earliest was founded as a Catholic church before being converted to Protestantism during the Reformation. It was replaced in the 18th century by a larger Baroque Lutheran building. Considered an outstanding example of Protestant sacred architecture, it featured one of the largest domes in Europe. It was originally built as a sign of the will of the citizens of Dresden to remain Protestant after their ruler had converted to Catholicism. description:
Buda Castle (Hungarian: Budavári Palota, German: Burgpalast) is the historical castle and palace complex of the Hungarian Kings in Budapest. It was first completed in 1265, although the massive Baroque palace today occupying most of the site was built between 1749 and 1769. The complex in the past was referred to as either the Royal Palace (Hungarian: Királyi-palota) or the Royal Castle (Hungarian: Királyi Vár, German: Königliche Burg). The castle now houses the Hungarian National Gallery and the Budapest Historical Museum.

Buda Castle sits on the southern tip of Castle Hill, surrounded by the touristic area known as Várnegyed (Castle Quarter), which is famous for its Medieval, Baroque, and Neoclassical houses, churches, public buildings, and monuments. The hill is linked to Clark Ádám Square and the Széchenyi Chain Bridge by the Castle Hill Funicular. The castle is a part of the Budapest World Heritage Site, so declared in 1987. The original Royal Palace was ruined during World War II; it was rebuilt in a simplified Stalinist Baroque style during the Kádár era.

title: The Memorial Pavilion That Honors Thailand's Tragic Queen Sunantha
tags: Bangkok|Thailand|Visit Thailand|Thailand tour guide|Thailand travel guide|Wat Ku|Wat Ku in Pak Kret|best places in Thailand.|Wat Phra Nang Rua Lom|Temples in Thailand|bangkok travel|thailand places to visit|travel thailand|nonthaburi thailand|thailand tourism
description:
Wat Ku is situated near the Chao Phraya River in Bang Pood Subdistrict, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi. The temple construction is of Mon architecture.

Wat Ku or Wat Phra Nang Rua Lom was built in 1752. It was formerly named Wat Lang Suan, but later, on May 31st, 1880, the royal yacht of Queen Sunantha Kumariratana, the first queen consort of King Rama V, passed by Bang Pa In, and the yacht sank, resulting in the deaths of Queen Sunantha Kumariratana and Queen Kannaporn Petchsopang.

Overview & Historical Significance
Origins & Architecture
Wat Ku was founded during the Thonburi era by Phraya Cheng (a Mon leader), reflecting Mon-style architecture and cultural heritage. Inside its old chapel, you'll find intricate mural paintings of the Mon tradition depicting scenes from the Buddha’s life 

Tragic Royal Connection
The temple is most well-known for its link to a sorrowful event: Queen Sunandha Kumariratana, consort of King Rama V, tragically drowned in the Chao Phraya River nearby while pregnant. At the time, strict laws prevented commoners from touching or aiding royalty, which ultimately contributed to the tragedy and were later repealed 

Memorial Pavilion & Relics
On the temple grounds is a memorial pavilion modeled after the Phra Thinang Aisawan Thippaya-Asana at Bang Pa-In Palace, built in remembrance of the Queen. The salvaged royal barge has been preserved in a structure beside the main hall, and a large reclining Buddha statue stands prominently inside the wihan (sanctuary)
.
Temporary Resting Place for Royal Remains
Wat Ku served as the temporary location where Queen Sunandha’s body was brought before being transported to the Grand Palace for lying-in-state. This event contributed to the temple’s name—“Ku,” meaning “to recover” or “to salvage,”—symbolizing both the recovery of the royal vessel and her remains.

Camphor Clay Pots on Koh Kret: A Glimpse into Tradition
Artisanal Heritage
Koh Kret, located in the Chao Phraya River of Nonthaburi Province, is celebrated for pottery crafted by the Mon community—descendants of migrant Mon people. Pottery is their signature vocation, passed down through generations and woven into local identity.

Distinctive Style & Technique
One notable style feature is red-and-black glazed surfaces and intricate designs characteristic of Mon craftsmanship.
These pots—often used as incense burners or decorative vessels—exhibit elegant perforations and ornate forms that combine functionality with artistry, as beautifully depicted in the images above.

Crafting Process & Community
Visitors to Koh Kret can witness pottery-making up close: artisans molding clay on wheels, engraving patterns by hand, and firing the pieces in traditional kilns. This craft is also championed under Thailand’s “One Tambon One Product” (OTOP) program, promoting local specialties across the country

What to Explore There
Pottery Village Stalls: Along the weekend market path, you’ll find stalls filled with handmade items—plates, cups, teapots, incense burners, and iconic charcoal-heated hotpot sets.

Cultural Immersion: Beyond pottery, you'll experience Mon culture, delicious local foods (like khao chae and Mon-style fritters), and peaceful riverside ambiance.

Worth a Visit?
Absolutely—especially if you're drawn to authentic handmade crafts and cultural experiences. Koh Kret offers a rare opportunity to purchase traditional pottery directly from the makers, supporting the community and acquiring one-of-a-kind souvenirs. As one Redditor noted:

Cochrane was founded in 1954 (as Pueblo Nuevo), but didn't have road access to the rest of Chile until 1988, when the Carretera Austral was opened. The town was later named Cochrane in honour of Thomas Cochrane, 10th Earl of Dundonald, a British naval captain and radical politician who was appointed the first Admiral of Chile.

The Confluencia Río Baker/Neff is a striking natural wonder in Chile's Aysén region, where the intense turquoise, glacier-fed Baker River meets the murky, sediment-rich Neff River. Villa O'Higgins is the remote, southernmost town on Chile's Carretera Austral (Route 7), serving as the final, dramatic destination of this 1,247+ km Patagonian highway. Situated near the O'Higgins Glacier and Southern Patagonian Ice Field, it is a hub for eco-tourism, trekking, and, since 1999, the gateway for overland, cross-border adventures to El Chaltén, Argentina.

Patagonia National Park (Spanish: Parque Nacional Patagonia) is a national park in the Aysén Region of Chile. Once a private nature reserve operated as a public-access park, it was donated to the government of Chile by Tompkins Conservation in 2018.

The heart of the park is the Chacabuco Valley, an ecologically significant east-west valley that forms a pass over the Andes Mountains, resulting in a transition zone between the Patagonian steppe grasslands of Argentine Patagonia and the southern beech forests of Chilean Patagonia to the west. It is located between General Carrera Lake to the north and Cochrane Lake to the south and extends to the Argentine border to the east. The park contains a network of trails and campgrounds, as well as a visitor center.

description:
The story of Farellones began in the late 1930s when skiing was still a relatively new sport in Chile. A small group of passionate skiers dreamed of creating a place where families and athletes could enjoy the mountains during winter.

By the 1940s, Farellones had grown into Chile's very first ski village. Wooden cabins, cozy lodges, and simple ski slopes welcomed visitors from Santiago, only about an hour's drive away. Over the decades, Farellones became the birthplace of modern skiing in Chile. Even today, many Chilean families bring their children here to learn skiing and snowboarding for the very first time.

As Chile's popularity as a winter destination continued to grow, an even bigger vision emerged.

In 1988, Valle Nevado Ski Resort officially opened its doors. Inspired by some of Europe's most famous Alpine resorts, Valle Nevado was designed as a world-class ski destination. Located more than 3,000 meters above sea level, it offers breathtaking panoramic views, modern hotels, and hundreds of hectares of ski terrain.

Today, Valle Nevado attracts visitors from all over the world. Professional skiers, snowboarders, photographers, and travelers come here every winter to experience the powder snow and the spectacular scenery of the Andes.
